Senior leaders are gone. Several of its correspondents have vanished. Can the newsmagazine survive under Bari Weiss and Nick Bilton?

On Tuesday night, Scott Pelley sat in his office, huddled with his “60 Minutes” producers, waiting for a resolution to a fight with the top leaders at CBS News and his new executive producer.

He was supposed to be on vacation. After all, “60 Minutes” goes on hiatus in the summer, and correspondents typically plan for the new season, which picks up in the fall.
